source.title: Left Ventricular Function, Congestion, and Effect of Empagliflozin on Heart Failure Risk After Myocardial Infarction
source.journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
source.source_type: prespecified secondary analysis of an international randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial

large_source_decision: Semantic batching used because the paper plus supplement contain multiple endpoint families, subgroup forest plots, recurrent-event analyses, safety tables, and supplemental figures that require separate reconciliation.
reference_range: Main PDF journal pages 2245-2246; bibliography treated as provenance infrastructure and exported separately.

main_visuals.representation: structured summary of continuous-LVEF spline risk
structured treatment-effect tables by LVEF and congestion
continuous-LVEF interaction P values and interpretation

supplement_visuals.representation: congestion symptoms, signs, and treatment counts
baseline characteristics by LVEF; key differences summarized
baseline characteristics by congestion; key differences summarized
selected safety outcomes overall and by LVEF
overall exploratory HF adverse-event effects plus heterogeneity summary

coverage_decisions.baseline_tables: Not atomized cell-by-cell. The atom set preserves population-defining counts and the source's central baseline contrasts. SEA reconciles the full tables at the result-family level.
coverage_decisions.combined_subgroup_forest_plot: The highest-risk placebo category and the cross-category trend are atomized. All treatment forest-plot LVEF and congestion rows are atomized. Five-way combined treatment rows are preserved in SEA rather than emitted as 15 additional near-duplicate atoms.
coverage_decisions.bibliography: 28 references exported to Markdown and not atomized.
coverage_decisions.disclosures: Funding and the existence/nature of extensive author conflicts are atomized; individual financial relationships are not split into one atom per company.

source_integrity_findings.finding: The congestion column is printed as 19.8 ±14.6 mmHg while the no-congestion column is 73.5 ±9.9 mmHg with P=0.5082. The value is internally implausible and inconsistent with the surrounding blood-pressure data. It was not silently corrected or used as an extracted quantitative atom.

omissions_and_reasons: No bibliography entries were treated as study-generated evidence.
No unreported subgroup values, missing confidence intervals, or mechanistic effects were reconstructed.
No external current-practice verification was added because @VERIFY was not activated.
